title: Family Wellness & Nutrition
subtitle: A plate, not a list. And who actually decides what you eat.
objectives: Name the Go, Grow and Glow groups
Describe the proportions of Pinggang Pinoy
Explain why each group is needed
Describe habits that support family wellness

cards.title: A plate, not a list
cards.text: A list of food groups tells you what exists. A plate tells you how much. And how much is the part that actually decides anything.

cards.title: Three jobs on one plate
cards.text: Each group does something the others cannot.
points: **Go**: energy. Rice, bread, root crops.
**Grow**: building material. Fish, meat, egg, beans, milk.
**Glow**: vitamins and minerals. Vegetables and fruit.
**Water** sits beside the plate, not on it.

cards.title: The plate, split into Go, Grow, Glow and water
cards.text: Pinggang Pinoy is a proportion. Tap each part and read the share.

question.text: Which group should take the biggest share of the plate?
question.explain: Vegetables and fruit. About half the plate.

cards.title: Go is not the enemy
cards.text: Energy food gets blamed, and it is what the training runs on.
points: **Without Go, you cannot train.** You run out mid-session.
**Without Grow, you train and do not rebuild.**
**Without Glow, both of the above work badly.**
**The question is proportion**, never which one to delete.

cards.title: GO: what the training runs on
cards.alt: Steamed rice, pandesal, kamote, cassava and boiled saba banana arranged on a pale surface
cards.text: Rice, pandesal, kamote, cassava, saba. Energy, and not the enemy.

cards.title: You rebuild while asleep, not while training
cards.text: Training is the request. Food and sleep are the build.
points: **Training breaks tissue down.**
**Protein and sleep put it back stronger.**
**Skip either and the session was wasted.**
**Eight to ten hours** at your age, not six.

cards.title: GROW: the smallest share
cards.alt: A whole bangus, boiled eggs, monggo beans, chicken, tofu and a glass of milk arranged on a pale surface
cards.text: Bangus, egg, monggo, chicken, tofu, milk. Smallest on the plate, still essential.

question.text: Where does water belong on Pinggang Pinoy?
question.explain: Six to eight glasses a day, more when you train.

cards.title: It is a household system, not a personal one
cards.text: Most of what you eat is decided before you are hungry.
points: **What is in the kitchen** decides most meals.
**Eating together** makes portions visible.
**A shared schedule** protects sleep.
**One person's habit** becomes everyone's default.

cards.title: Fuel, parts and coolant
cards.text: The analogy holds further than it has any right to.
points: **Go is the fuel.** No fuel, no laps.
**Grow is the spare parts.** That is how worn components get replaced.
**Glow is the oil and coolant**: nothing moves without it.
**Water is water.** An overheating engine and an overheating runner need the same thing.

cards.title: GLOW: half the plate
cards.alt: Kangkong, halved papaya, mangoes, ampalaya, pechay and calamansi arranged on a pale surface
cards.text: Kangkong, papaya, mango, ampalaya, pechay, calamansi. The biggest share.

cards.title: Making weight is not the same as being fit
cards.text: Cutting water weight is a real practice and a real risk.
points: **A fighter can lose kilos in days** and most of it is water.
**Performance drops with it.**
**That is why weigh-ins are a day early** in many codes.
**Weight is one number.** It is not the verdict.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Go for energy, Grow for building, Glow for vitamins and minerals.
Glow takes about half the plate; Grow the smallest share.
Water sits beside the plate: six to eight glasses, more when training.
You rebuild during sleep, not during the session.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 8 MAPEH, Health strand. Pinggang Pinoy is taught as a proportion rather than a list of groups, because proportion is the part that changes behaviour and a tappable plate shows it directly. The week deliberately defends Go, since 'carbohydrates are bad' is the belief a boy who trains is most likely to pick up and the one that will cost him sessions. Family wellness is framed as a household system (what is in the kitchen decides most meals) rather than as willpower. The boxing lens handles weight-cutting honestly: it is real, it is mostly water, and performance drops with it.
discussion: Ask him to lay out one meal in the right proportions.
Ask what is in the kitchen right now and what that means for this week's meals.
Ask why a weigh-in is often a day before a fight.
extension: Have him plan and serve one family meal against the plate.
Have him track water for three days and compare with the target.
misconceptions: "Carbohydrates are the problem." Without them you cannot train.
"Protein alone builds muscle." Sleep does the building.
"Weight is the measure of fitness." It is one number out of five.
